subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo — TTFT & streaming requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful. A few follow-up items from our side so we can scope the integration and procurement:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target is <= 150ms for our short prompts (~32 tokens). Mobile clients are especially sensitive.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients, but we have native mobile apps where WebSocket might be better.
- Chunk cadence: ideally ~200-300ms for progressive UX (we want visible partial updates every ~250ms).
- Concurrency & throughput: estimated steady-state 150 req/s across our EU+US fleet, with bursts up to 500 req/s during peak campaigns. Concurrency per model instance TBD — we can provide load distribution details.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these TTFT and streaming cadence targets on a standard Dedicated instance (no custom kernels)? Also need a short plan for how you'd validate during PoC — what logs/metrics you'll provide and what telemetry we should collect on our side.

Attaching our initial requirements spreadsheet (acme-ttft-requirements.xlsx).

Best,
John

Hi John — thanks for the clear requirements and for the spreadsheet. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap of targets you called out:
- TTFT: <= 150ms (32-token prompts)
- Streaming: browser: SSE preferred; mobile: considering WebSocket
- Chunk cadence: ~200–300ms (250ms target)
- Throughput: steady 150 req/s, burst to 500 req/s
- Region: US + EU (low cross-region noise)

What we can commit to now (high level):
- Redwood Dedicated (standard config) commonly achieves sub-150ms TTFT for 32-token prompts on our 80GB GPU config when models are warm and KV cache is available. Exact numbers depend on model size/quantization and sequence length — we will characterize this in the PoC.
- Streaming: we support both SSE and WebSocket with identical chunking behavior; SSE is slightly simpler for browser clients, WebSocket avoids some mobile proxy issues.
- Chunk cadence: we can tune token batching and flush cadence to aim for ~200–300ms per chunk; we'll include a suggested cadence control for your engineers to test.
- Concurrency/throughput: Dedicated pools can be configured to handle steady 150 req/s and bursts to 500 req/s; we'll propose autoscale and burst policies in the MAP.

Requested from you:
1) Confirm whether SSE is preferable for the majority of your traffic or if we should plan for WebSocket-first for mobile.
2) Share a couple of representative prompt payloads (we'll use them for perf runs).
3) Any compliance items (SOC2, data residency) to surface early?

Next steps proposed:
- Rishi (cc'd) will draft a PoC test plan (latency/TTFT measurement, streaming chunk cadence, concurrency tests) and a checklist of telemetry we need from Acme.
- We'll run an initial perf validation against a staging Dedicated pool using your sample prompts and share detailed latency histograms (P50/P90/P99), first-byte timings, and SSE chunk timing distributions.
- Schedule a 60-min technical run-through next week. Proposed slots: Thu 23 Jul 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 24 Jul 14:00–15:00 PT.

Attaching our streaming implementation note that covers SSE vs WebSocket and flush cadence tuning (redwood-sse-tech-note.pdf).

If that sounds good, confirm the slot and send the sample prompts and any procurement contact notes. I'll loop in Naomi on commercial and SOW.

Thanks — Marissa

John — looping in Rishi (Sales Engineer) and Naomi (AE) as discussed. Thanks for confirming the prompt upload; we reviewed the samples and have the following proposed Mutual Action Plan for the PoC: 

1) Objectives (2 weeks):
   - Validate TTFT <= 150ms for 32-token prompts (warm cache) across US/EU nodes.
   - Verify streaming chunk cadence ~200–300ms under steady and burst conditions.
   - Confirm autoscale/burst configuration can handle 500 req/s bursts without TTFT regression beyond agreed SLO.

2) Test plan (Rishi to lead):
   - Baseline: run 10k small-prompt requests to establish P50/P90/P99 TTFT and initial first-byte timings.
   - Streaming cadence: instrument SSE/WebSocket streams, measure inter-chunk latency distribution, flush behavior, and perceived UX latency.
   - Concurrency sweep: ramp to 150 req/s sustained, then simulate burst to 500 req/s for 2 minutes — measure degradation curves and recovery time.
   - Telemetry: Redwood will provide per-request TTFT, token-first-byte time, token-flush cadence histograms, and server-side CPU/GPU utilization. Acme to provide client-side RTT and perceived latency samples from representative mobile devices.

3) Deliverables (end of PoC):
   - Latency histograms (P50/P90/P99), TTFT breakdown by region, per-chunk cadence CSV, recommended config for Dedicated pool (batching, cache window, flush cadence).
   - Suggested changes to app integration (SSE vs WebSocket guidance per platform).
   - Short SOW + pricing for 3-month PoC (Naomi to send today).

4) Schedule:
   - Technical run-through (60m): Mon 2 Aug 10:00–11:00 PT — please confirm.
   - Initial perf run start: Tue 3 Aug.

Rishi — can you confirm the exact test harness we'll use (k6 or internal runner + our perf harness) and whether we need any special tokens/whitelisted IPs? Also propose the initial Dedicated pool config (GPU type, approx reserved QPS).

Naomi — I'll rely on you for the SOW and commercial estimate for the PoC; procurement is cc'd.

Thanks all — excited to get this running.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
